The subject-level ADaM dataset (`ADSL`), built end-to-end from SDTM in polars. It
reproduces the derivation flow of the
[pharmaverse ADSL example](https://pharmaverse.github.io/examples/adam/adsl.html),
which uses `{admiral}` + `{metatools}` + `{metacore}`, minus its metadata/XPT step (that
is about SAS transport files, not data). Where this study's shipped
[ADaM ADSL](../datasets/pharmaverseadam/adsl.html) carries the same variable, the result is checked
against it.

The blocks run as the page is rendered, so what appears under one is what the code
printed; a block that stops running stops the render.

```{python}
from functools import reduce

import polars as pl

from pharmadata import pharmaverseadam as adam, pharmaversesdtm as sdtm
```

## Load the SDTM inputs

`dm`, `ds`, `ex`, `ae` and `suppdm` are the domains the derivations read from. The R
example also loads `vs`, but no ADSL variable here uses it.

```{python}
dm = sdtm.dm
ds = sdtm.ds
ex = sdtm.ex
ae = sdtm.ae
suppdm = sdtm.suppdm
```

## DM + SUPPDM

The R example starts with `metatools::combine_supp()`, which transposes `SUPPDM` so each
`QNAM` becomes a column and each `QVAL` its value, then joins the result onto `DM`.
`pivot()` is the polars spelling of that transpose. This study's `SUPPDM` holds only the
six population flags (`ITT`, `SAFETY`, `EFFICACY`, `COMPLT8/16/24`), none of which appear
in the shipped ADSL, so nothing after this step reads them; the step is kept because it is
the first one the R guide performs.

```{python}
supp_wide = suppdm.pivot(
    values="QVAL", index=["STUDYID", "USUBJID"], on="QNAM", aggregate_function="first"
)
dm_suppdm = dm.join(supp_wide, on=["STUDYID", "USUBJID"], how="left")
```

## The columns that carry straight through

`build_from_derived()` pulls the `DM` columns whose SDTM name is also their ADaM name.
Here that is every `DM` column except the three SDTM-only ones (`DOMAIN`, `ARMNRS`,
`ACTARMUD`).

```{python}
adsl = dm.select([c for c in dm.columns if c not in ("DOMAIN", "ARMNRS", "ACTARMUD")])
```

## Grouping variables

`admiral::derive_vars_cat()` applies a lookup table of conditions in order: the first
condition that holds wins, the rest are never tested. A chain of `pl.when().then()` is
exactly that, so one small function walks the lookup rows and stacks a `when` per row.

```{python}
def derive_vars_cat(df: pl.DataFrame, lookup: pl.DataFrame) -> pl.DataFrame:
    """Add one column per lookup column, from the first condition that holds."""
    rows = lookup.to_dicts()

    def chain(target: str) -> pl.Expr:
        first = pl.when(rows[0]["condition"]).then(pl.lit(rows[0][target]))
        folded = reduce(
            lambda acc, row: acc.when(row["condition"]).then(pl.lit(row[target])),
            rows[1:],
            first,
        )
        return folded.otherwise(pl.lit(None)).alias(target)

    targets = [column for column in lookup.columns if column != "condition"]
    return df.with_columns(*(chain(target) for target in targets))


agegr1_lookup = pl.DataFrame(
    {
        "condition": [
            pl.col("AGE").is_null(),
            pl.col("AGE") < 18,
            pl.col("AGE").is_between(18, 64),
            pl.col("AGE").is_not_null(),
        ],
        "AGEGR1": ["Missing", "<18", "18-64", ">64"],
        "AGEGR1N": [4, 1, 2, 3],
    },
    schema_overrides={"condition": pl.Object},
)

adsl = derive_vars_cat(adsl, agegr1_lookup)
```

A column of expressions is not a type Arrow can store, hence `pl.Object`: the lookup is a
definition read by the derivation, not data it works on. `AGE` is present for all 306
subjects and all are adults, so only the `18-64` and `>64` groups are populated.

The numeric `RACEN` comes from a controlled codelist in the R example
(`metatools::create_var_from_codelist`). The codes live in the study's terminology, which
is not shipped with the data, so a simple 1..4 stands in here:

```{python}
race_codelist = {
    "AMERICAN INDIAN OR ALASKA NATIVE": 1,
    "ASIAN": 2,
    "BLACK OR AFRICAN AMERICAN": 3,
    "WHITE": 4,
}
adsl = adsl.with_columns(pl.col("RACE").replace_strict(race_codelist, default=None).alias("RACEN"))
```

## Exposure derivations

Treatment start and end come from `EX`, after `EXSTDTC`/`EXENDTC` are turned into
datetimes. Here every exposure datetime is a date with no time part, so the time is
imputed: first moment of the day for a start, last moment for an end, with the imputation
flag `H` (hour was the highest unit imputed). `admiral::derive_vars_dtm` would read a
partial time from the `--T--` part of the ISO string and lower that flag accordingly; with
date-only strings the flag is always `H`.

```{python}
ex_ext = ex.with_columns(
    pl.col("EXSTDTC").str.to_datetime("%Y-%m-%d").alias("EXSTDTM"),
    pl.lit("H").alias("EXSTTMF"),
    (
        pl.col("EXENDTC").str.to_datetime("%Y-%m-%d")
        + pl.duration(hours=23, minutes=59, seconds=59)
    ).alias("EXENDTM"),
    pl.lit("H").alias("EXENTMF"),
)
```

`derive_vars_merged()` is the polars form of `admiral::derive_vars_merged()`: filter the
source, order it, take the first or last row per subject, rename the wanted columns and
left-join them onto the main dataset. `order_by` plus `mode="first"` is "the earliest
record"; `mode="last"` is "the latest". A `missing_values` mapping fills only the subjects
whose join found no row - a cell that is null because the source held null stays null.

```{python}
def derive_vars_merged(
    dataset: pl.DataFrame,
    dataset_add: pl.DataFrame,
    by_vars: list[str],
    new_vars: dict[str, str],
    filter_add: pl.Expr | None = None,
    order_by: list[str] | None = None,
    mode: str = "first",
    missing_values: dict[str, str] | None = None,
) -> pl.DataFrame:
    add = dataset_add.filter(filter_add) if filter_add is not None else dataset_add
    if order_by is not None:
        add = add.sort(order_by)
    agg = pl.all().first() if mode == "first" else pl.all().last()
    add = add.group_by(by_vars).agg(agg)
    keep = by_vars + list(new_vars.values())
    add = add.select(keep).rename({src: tgt for tgt, src in new_vars.items()})
    add = add.with_columns(pl.lit(True).alias("__matched__"))
    out = dataset.join(add, on=by_vars, how="left")
    for target, fill in (missing_values or {}).items():
        out = out.with_columns(
            pl.when(pl.col("__matched__").is_null())
            .then(pl.lit(fill))
            .otherwise(pl.col(target))
            .alias(target)
        )
    return out.drop("__matched__")
```

Only dosing records count: a positive dose, or a zero dose of placebo. `TRTSDTM` is the
first such record, `TRTEDTM` the last. From the two datetimes come the dates, the start
time and the treatment duration (`TRTDURD = TRTEDT - TRTSDT + 1`). `SAFFL` is `Y` for a
subject with any dosing record and `N` otherwise - `derive_var_merged_exist_flag()` in the
R example, a left join of the safety subjects here.

```{python}
dose_ok = (pl.col("EXDOSE") > 0) | (
    (pl.col("EXDOSE") == 0) & pl.col("EXTRT").str.contains("PLACEBO")
)

adsl = derive_vars_merged(
    adsl,
    ex_ext,
    ["STUDYID", "USUBJID"],
    {"TRTSDTM": "EXSTDTM", "TRTSTMF": "EXSTTMF"},
    filter_add=dose_ok & pl.col("EXSTDTM").is_not_null(),
    order_by=["EXSTDTM", "EXSEQ"],
    mode="first",
)
adsl = derive_vars_merged(
    adsl,
    ex_ext,
    ["STUDYID", "USUBJID"],
    {"TRTEDTM": "EXENDTM", "TRTETMF": "EXENTMF"},
    filter_add=dose_ok & pl.col("EXENDTM").is_not_null(),
    order_by=["EXENDTM", "EXSEQ"],
    mode="last",
)
```

```{python}
adsl = adsl.with_columns(
    pl.col("TRTSDTM").dt.date().alias("TRTSDT"),
    pl.col("TRTEDTM").dt.date().alias("TRTEDT"),
    pl.col("TRTSDTM").dt.time().alias("TRTSTM"),
)
adsl = adsl.with_columns(
    ((pl.col("TRTEDT") - pl.col("TRTSDT")).dt.total_days() + 1)
    .cast(pl.Float64)
    .alias("TRTDURD"),
)

safety_ids = (
    ex.filter(dose_ok)
    .select(["STUDYID", "USUBJID"])
    .unique()
    .with_columns(pl.lit("Y").alias("SAFFL"))
)
adsl = adsl.join(safety_ids, on=["STUDYID", "USUBJID"], how="left").with_columns(
    pl.col("SAFFL").fill_null("N")
)
```

## Treatment variables

The example's mapping for a study without periods: subjects in `Screen Failure`,
`Not Assigned` or `Not Treated` get `No Treatment`, everyone else keeps their arm. The
numeric versions are a codelist again.

```{python}
def no_treatment(col: str) -> pl.Expr:
    return (
        (pl.col(col) == "Screen Failure")
        | (pl.col(col) == "Not Assigned")
        | (pl.col(col) == "Not Treated")
    )


adsl = adsl.with_columns(
    pl.when(no_treatment("ARM")).then(pl.lit("No Treatment")).otherwise(pl.col("ARM")).alias("TRT01P"),
    pl.when(no_treatment("ACTARM")).then(pl.lit("No Treatment")).otherwise(pl.col("ACTARM")).alias("TRT01A"),
)

trt_codelist = {
    "No Treatment": 0,
    "Placebo": 1,
    "Xanomeline High Dose": 2,
    "Xanomeline Low Dose": 3,
}
adsl = adsl.with_columns(
    pl.col("TRT01P").replace_strict(trt_codelist, default=None).alias("TRT01PN"),
    pl.col("TRT01A").replace_strict(trt_codelist, default=None).alias("TRT01AN"),
)
```

## Disposition variables

`DSSTDTC` becomes a date once, and the resulting `DSSTDT` is what every disposition date
is picked out of: `EOSDT` from the end-of-study disposition, `RANDDT` from the
randomization milestone, `SCRFDT` from the screen-failure event, `FRVDT` from the final
retrieval visit.

```{python}
ds_ext = ds.with_columns(pl.col("DSSTDTC").str.to_date("%Y-%m-%d").alias("DSSTDT"))

adsl = derive_vars_merged(
    adsl,
    ds_ext,
    ["STUDYID", "USUBJID"],
    {"EOSDT": "DSSTDT"},
    filter_add=(pl.col("DSCAT") == "DISPOSITION EVENT") & (pl.col("DSDECOD") != "SCREEN FAILURE"),
)
```

`EOSSTT` maps `DSDECOD` to `COMPLETED`/`DISCONTINUED`, with `SCREEN FAILURE` mapped to
null. The `missing_values` "ONGOING" fills only a subject with no disposition event at
all - not the screen failures, whose null is a derived value.

```{python}
ds_eosstt = ds.with_columns(
    pl.when(pl.col("DSDECOD") == "COMPLETED")
    .then(pl.lit("COMPLETED"))
    .when(pl.col("DSDECOD") == "SCREEN FAILURE")
    .then(pl.lit(None))
    .otherwise(pl.lit("DISCONTINUED"))
    .alias("EOSSTT_src")
)
adsl = derive_vars_merged(
    adsl,
    ds_eosstt,
    ["STUDYID", "USUBJID"],
    {"EOSSTT": "EOSSTT_src"},
    filter_add=pl.col("DSCAT") == "DISPOSITION EVENT",
    missing_values={"EOSSTT": "ONGOING"},
)
```

`DTHDT` is `DTHDTC` as a date; every death date in this study is complete, so the
`highest_imputation="M"` the R example sets (impute missing month/day to the first) never
fires here. The relative day of death counts from first dose (`+ 1`); days from last dose
to death do not.

```{python}
adsl = adsl.with_columns(pl.col("DTHDTC").str.to_date("%Y-%m-%d").alias("DTHDT"))

adsl = derive_vars_merged(
    adsl,
    ds_ext,
    ["STUDYID", "USUBJID"],
    {"RANDDT": "DSSTDT"},
    filter_add=pl.col("DSDECOD") == "RANDOMIZED",
)
adsl = derive_vars_merged(
    adsl,
    ds_ext,
    ["STUDYID", "USUBJID"],
    {"SCRFDT": "DSSTDT"},
    filter_add=(pl.col("DSCAT") == "DISPOSITION EVENT") & (pl.col("DSDECOD") == "SCREEN FAILURE"),
)
adsl = derive_vars_merged(
    adsl,
    ds_ext,
    ["STUDYID", "USUBJID"],
    {"FRVDT": "DSSTDT"},
    filter_add=(pl.col("DSCAT") == "OTHER EVENT") & (pl.col("DSDECOD") == "FINAL RETRIEVAL VISIT"),
)

adsl = adsl.with_columns(
    ((pl.col("DTHDT") - pl.col("TRTSDT")).dt.total_days() + 1).cast(pl.Float64).alias("DTHADY"),
    (pl.col("DTHDT") - pl.col("TRTEDT")).dt.total_days().cast(pl.Float64).alias("LDDTHELD"),
    pl.when(pl.col("RANDDT").is_not_null()).then(pl.lit("Y")).otherwise(pl.lit(None)).alias("RANDFL"),
)
```

## Cause of death

`DTHCAUS` comes from whichever domain collected it, with `DTHDOM` recording that domain.
`admiral::derive_vars_extreme_event()` stacks the candidate events and takes the first;
the polars equivalent is a `concat` of the two event frames ordered by an event number,
then one row per subject. A fatal AE contributes its `AEDECOD`; a `DS` death whose term
starts "DEATH DUE TO" would contribute `DSTERM` - in this study every `DS` death term is
just "DEATH", so the cause always comes from `AE`.

```{python}
ae_event = ae.filter(pl.col("AEOUT") == "FATAL").select(
    "STUDYID", "USUBJID",
    pl.col("AEDECOD").alias("DTHCAUS"),
    pl.lit("AE").alias("DTHDOM"),
    pl.lit(1).alias("event_nr"),
)
ds_event = ds.filter(
    (pl.col("DSDECOD") == "DEATH") & pl.col("DSTERM").str.contains("DEATH DUE TO")
).select(
    "STUDYID", "USUBJID",
    pl.col("DSTERM").alias("DTHCAUS"),
    pl.lit("DS").alias("DTHDOM"),
    pl.lit(2).alias("event_nr"),
)
events = (
    pl.concat([ae_event, ds_event])
    .sort("event_nr")
    .unique(subset=["STUDYID", "USUBJID"], keep="first")
)
adsl = adsl.join(events.drop("event_nr"), on=["STUDYID", "USUBJID"], how="left")
```

## Other grouping variables

The same `derive_vars_cat()` makes the remaining groups: region, race and the cause-of-
death category. The lookups are the R example's, conditions and values alike.

```{python}
region1_lookup = pl.DataFrame(
    {
        "condition": [
            (pl.col("COUNTRY") == "CAN") | (pl.col("COUNTRY") == "USA"),
            pl.col("COUNTRY").is_not_null(),
            pl.col("COUNTRY").is_null(),
        ],
        "REGION1": ["North America", "Rest of the World", "Missing"],
        "REGION1N": [1, 2, 3],
    },
    schema_overrides={"condition": pl.Object},
)
racegr1_lookup = pl.DataFrame(
    {
        "condition": [
            pl.col("RACE") == "WHITE",
            pl.col("RACE") != "WHITE",
            pl.col("RACE").is_null(),
        ],
        "RACEGR1": ["White", "Non-white", "Missing"],
        "RACEGR1N": [1, 2, 3],
    },
    schema_overrides={"condition": pl.Object},
)
dthcgr1_lookup = pl.DataFrame(
    {
        "condition": [
            pl.col("DTHDOM") == "AE",
            pl.col("DTHDOM").is_not_null() & pl.col("DTHCAUS").str.contains("PROGRESSIVE DISEASE|DISEASE RELAPSE"),
            pl.col("DTHDOM").is_not_null() & pl.col("DTHCAUS").is_not_null(),
            pl.col("DTHDOM").is_null(),
        ],
        "DTHCGR1": ["ADVERSE EVENT", "PROGRESSIVE DISEASE", "OTHER", None],
        "DTHCGR1N": [1, 2, 3, None],
    },
    schema_overrides={"condition": pl.Object},
)
adsl = derive_vars_cat(adsl, region1_lookup)
adsl = derive_vars_cat(adsl, racegr1_lookup)
adsl = derive_vars_cat(adsl, dthcgr1_lookup)
```

## Check it against the shipped ADSL

The package ships both ends of the derivation, so the result is checked against the
study's own ADSL with `datacompy`. Every derived variable that the shipped ADSL carries
with the same encoding is compared; the report lists any mismatches per column.

```{python}
import datacompy

shipped = adam.adsl

compare = [
    "AGEGR1", "RACEGR1", "DTHCGR1", "DTHDOM", "DTHCAUS", "EOSSTT", "EOSDT",
    "RANDDT", "SCRFDT", "FRVDT", "DTHDT", "DTHADY", "LDDTHELD", "TRTSDT",
    "TRTEDT", "TRTDURD", "SAFFL",
]

cmp = datacompy.PolarsCompare(
    df1=adsl.select(["USUBJID", *compare]),
    df2=shipped.select(["USUBJID", *compare]),
    join_columns="USUBJID",
    df1_name="derived",
    df2_name="shipped",
)

mismatch_df = cmp.all_mismatch()
mismatches = {
    col: mismatch_df.filter(
        pl.col(f"{col.lower()}_derived") != pl.col(f"{col.lower()}_shipped")
    ).height
    for col in compare
}

print(cmp.report())
```

Two derived variables are deliberately absent from that list because this study's ADSL
encodes them differently:

- **`TRT01P`/`TRT01A`.** The example's generic mapping turns screen failures into
  `No Treatment`; the shipped ADSL keeps `Screen Failure`. Every other arm matches.
- **`REGION1`.** The example derives `North America`; the shipped ADSL abbreviates it to
  `NA`.

The numeric companions (`AGEGR1N`, `RACEN`, `TRT01PN`, `TRT01AN`, `REGION1N`, `RACEGR1N`,
`DTHCGR1N`) and `TRTSTM`, `RANDFL` have no counterpart among the shipped ADSL's 55
variables, so nothing can be checked for them.

The derived dataset itself, for reference:

```{python}
print(adsl.shape)
print(adsl.select(["USUBJID", "TRTSDT", "TRTEDT", "TRTDURD", "SAFFL", "EOSSTT", "DTHCAUS", "DTHCGR1"]).head(5))
```
